verdicts.question: What are current Indian trade prices (Rs per kg or per tonne, with date and source) for the intermediate materials the refined chain adds at levels L3 to L5, which published sources exist for each, how often they move, and which may be shown on a public price board without a licence?
verdicts.problems: (1) Source check not possible in this pass: outbound fetches are refused (gateway 403 on 5paisa.com, alcircle.com, steel-baba.com, chemanalyst.com) and the session's WebSearch budget is exhausted, so none of the 55 cited snippets could be re-searched; every figure below the 'not confirmed by snippet' line stays unverified and must be re-run when the network setting is fixed. (2) Fly ash is internally contradictory: 'India average USD 82/MT in Q2 2026' is about Rs 6,900-7,000/t (at Rs 85/USD), well above the quoted Rs 500-4,075/t range and the 'Class F Rs 1,600-2,500/t' seed; one of the two is a different product or basis (dry vs pond ash, delivered vs gate) and the answer does not say which. (3) MCX copper Rs 1,397.05/kg implies about USD 16,400/t, whereas every copper scrap listing cited (Rs 470-880/kg) implies USD 5,500-10,000/t; the answer resolves this by calling all listings stale on the strength of a single broker snippet; the benchmark should be read from mcxindia.com itself before anything is seeded as 'cathode = MCX'. (4) Lead is inverted: 'refined spot Rs 169.45/kg' sits below 'remelted ingot Rs 180/kg' and 'producer refined Rs 188-230/kg'; secondary remelt sells at a discount to 99.97% refined, so the metalscost figure is most likely an LME conversion and not an Indian ex-works price. (5) NALCO Rs 352-379/kg against ADC12 Rs 201-203/kg gives a ratio of 0.57, where ADC12 normally trades at roughly 0.85-0.95 of primary; the answer flags it but still prints the figure (Nexizo is a third-party aggregator; the NALCO circular was not found). (6) The C&D comparison mixes editions and units: recycled aggregate Rs 420/cum is DSR 2023, natural stone aggregate Rs 1,400/cum is DSR 2021; per tonne (about 1.5 t/cum) that is roughly Rs 280/t vs Rs 930/t, and the only Bengaluru gate price (Rs 350-400/t) is from a 2017 paper. A 'DSR 2025 edition' is asserted without a source. (7) The Hindustan Copper formula '(LME + USD 120-150 premium) x 1.058 x TT rate + Rs 3,300/t' is not confirmed by any snippet quoted; the multiplier and premium need reading from hindustancopper.com. (8) Pyrolysis carbon black at Rs 22/kg is set against virgin CB at USD 0.95-1.15/kg (Rs 81-98/kg) and rCB USD 445/t (Rs 38/kg) without saying the Rs 22 listing is unrefined char, not recovered CB. (9) Chain gap: the founder's pre-processor list includes e-waste dismantlers, battery breakers and used-oil re-refiners, but the answer has no price at all for e-waste fractions (PCB, cable-granulation copper, mixed plastics housing), for battery lead paste or plates, or for re-refined base oil, and no price for the saleable by-product lots the processing-record model requires (PP cap/ring flake from PET lines, label fraction, tyre steel wire). (10) The R-PET conversion USD 943/MT = Rs 78-79/kg implies an FX of Rs 83.5/USD; at a mid-2026 rate nearer Rs 85-86 it is Rs 80-81/kg (minor). (11) The MCX Data Feed Policy date (10 Jul 2026) and the BigMint/Polymerupdate terms are not confirmed by any snippet I could reach.
verdicts.correction: Keep the answer's structure (listing ranges as a seed, replaced by Luma's own 28-day medians), with these changes. Fly ash: show the listing band Rs 500-4,075/t only, drop the USD 82/MT line until ChemAnalyst's basis is read, and seed Class F at 'open: Rs 1,600-2,500/t listing, unreconciled with a USD 82/MT assessment'. Copper: do not seed cathode = MCX until the mcxindia.com quote is read directly; seed copper millberry and granule as 'open: needs 10 yard quotes' and show MCX only as a hand-typed daily benchmark with its own date. Lead: treat refined (99.97%) as the benchmark and remelted ingot as benchmark minus a discount set from yard quotes; drop the Rs 169.45 metalscost figure unless its basis (ex-works India vs LME conversion) is confirmed. Aluminium: keep ADC12 non-OEM Rs 201,000-203,000/t and OEM Rs 209,000-210,000/t as the only aluminium seeds; hold the NALCO primary figure as an open item until NALCO's own circular is read. C&D: compare like with like (DSR 2023 recycled 20 mm Rs 420/cum vs DSR 2023 natural, both per cum, and convert to Rs/t at the density used) and mark the Bengaluru Rs 350-400/t gate price as 2017 and stale; Rock Crystals must be phoned. Add the missing pre-processor outputs as open items with owner: e-waste PCB, cable-granulation copper and housing plastics (ask two Bengaluru authorised dismantlers), battery plates/paste (ask a KSPCB-authorised lead recycler), re-refined base oil (ask a registered re-refiner), PET-line PP cap flake and label fraction, tyre steel wire. Pyrolysis: show Rs 22/kg as 'pyrolysis char, unrefined', not rCB. Licence question: unchanged in substance, but mark MCX policy date, BigMint and Polymerupdate terms as unverified until read; counsel confirms. Status stays 'partly'; every other figure carries 'listing, not re-verified in sceptic pass' until the network is restored and the searches re-run.

verdicts.question: How do buyers price grade differences at L3-L5, and how should Luma.Green's price board and rate cards represent material state and grade so the same code is not quoted at two levels at once? Recommend the board's grade dimensions per family and the reference figures to seed with.
verdicts.problems: (1) The repo claim is wrong: 'adminPrices already stores a level (L1) per observation' - convex/adminPrices.ts is a query/mutation module, not a table; the level lives on priceObservations and priceBoards in convex/tables/priceEngine.ts (wired into the schema through convex/tables/index.ts), where vPriceLevel = L1 | L2 only, and priceBoards is already keyed (city, materialCode, level, date). The cited schema.ts source ('keyed by materialCode only') describes only the older referencePrices/marketPrices/rateCards tables and misses the price engine, so the 'fix is structural rather than new tables' recommendation is aimed at the wrong tables. (2) The proposed code scheme (PLA-PET-BOT, NFE-CU-MILL, FER-SHRED...) renames the 26 shipped codes (PAPER-NEWS, PLASTIC-PET, METAL-COPPER, RECYCLED-PET-FLAKE, RECYCLED-HDPE-GRANULE, RECYCLED-ALU-INGOT in convex/lib/catalogue.ts), and docs/plan.md says codes are 'never renamed or reused' and already carry three tiers (household/trade/industrial). (3) The founder's own L1-L5 table is ambiguous on pellets: the 'who pays whom' column makes recycler-to-manufacturer L4, but the state column lists 'granule' under L3 and reserves L4 for 'manufacturer-specification' (S8 compound). The answer silently picks L4 for pellets and also hard-maps each code to an allowed level set, which conflicts with its own rule 2 (derive level from roles). (4) 'Lead remelt Rs 180, refined Rs 170' seed is inverted (secondary remelt is priced below 99.97% refined), inherited from answer 1. (5) 'Copper cathode = MCX spot Rs 1,397' seed rests on one unconfirmed broker snippet (see verdict 1). (6) '40% recycled content mandated in food packaging from 1 Apr 2026' - the 40% for FY 2026-27 is the PWM (Amendment) Rules 2022 target for Category I rigid plastic packaging generally, not a food-packaging mandate; food-contact rPET is a separate FSSAI authorisation. Not confirmed by snippet either way. (7) Grade dimensions omit items the founder's process-chain CSV specifies: flake IV band (cold-washed 0.60-0.64, hot-washed 0.64-0.70), flake moisture <1%, bale contamination <=2-5%, and a lot kind {main output, by-product, residual} - the founder's model says residual waste is 'never mixed into normal saleable stock', so the board needs a field that keeps residual lots off the saleable board. (8) Premium arithmetic is loose: hot vs cold PET flake mids are Rs 72 vs Rs 53.5 (about Rs 18-19/kg), stated as Rs 20-30; the shredded-vs-HMS 'Rs 2/kg' compares Steel Baba (city unstated) with BigMint DAP Mumbai, not like for like. (9) None of the 20 cited snippets could be re-searched in this pass (network refused, search budget spent); the ADC12 OEM premium (Rs 6-9/kg by the ranges, Rs 7.5 at mid) and the FSSAI 17-plant figure are therefore not confirmed by snippet.
verdicts.correction: Structural recommendation, corrected to the actual code: (a) extend vPriceLevel in convex/tables/priceEngine.ts from L1|L2 to L1..L5 and add gradeKey (string, from a per-family enum in convex/lib/catalogue.ts) plus lotKind {main, byproduct, residual} to priceObservations, priceBoards and priceBands; make the priceBoards index (city, materialCode, gradeKey, level, date) with one row per day per key; residual lots never publish to the board. (b) Keep the existing code convention and never rename: add new codes for new forms in the same style (PLASTIC-PET-BALE, RECYCLED-PET-FLAKE-COLD, RECYCLED-PET-FLAKE-HOT, RECYCLED-PET-PELLET, METAL-IRON-SHRED, METAL-IRON-HMS, METAL-COPPER-MILLBERRY, METAL-COPPER-GRANULE, RECYCLED-ALU-ADC12, RECYCLED-RUBBER-CRUMB, RECYCLED-CND-RA20, RECYCLED-CND-MSAND), each with a state band (S1-S2 loose, S3 bale, S4-S5 flake, S7 pellet/ingot/crumb, S8 compound) and the existing materials.level tier (household -> L1, trade -> L2, industrial -> L3+). (c) Level on a price row is derived from seller and buyer roles of the trade (kabadiwala->household L1, yard->kabadiwala L2, pre-processor/recycler->yard L3, recycler/compounder->manufacturer L4, manufacturer->industrial buyer L5); the code's tier is only a sanity check, and the founder should be asked to settle whether S7 granules sold recycler-to-manufacturer sit at L3 (state column) or L4 (who-pays-whom column) - recommend L4 by role, with the state field carrying S7, and say so in the plan. (d) Rate cards stay L1 (shop->household) and L2 (yard->shop); L3-L5 show as reference medians only. Grade dimensions as proposed, plus: PET flakes add IV band {0.60-0.64, 0.64-0.70, >0.70} and moisture {<1%, unknown}; bales add contamination band {<=2%, <=5%, unknown}; every family adds lotKind. Seeds: keep the plastics, ferrous, ADC12, crumb, tyre oil, cullet, C&D, paper and bio by-product mids as 'listing, not re-verified', with three changes: copper cathode and millberry/granule = open until the MCX quote is read from mcxindia.com and 10 yard quotes are in; lead = refined benchmark open, remelt = refined minus a yard-quoted discount (do not seed Rs 180/Rs 170); fly ash = open (listing Rs 1,600-2,500/t conflicts with a USD 82/MT assessment). Replace the FSSAI sentence with: food-contact rPET may only be sold as such by an FSSAI-authorised plant; the 40% FY 2026-27 recycled-content target is the PWM Rules Category I rigid-packaging obligation (confirm on cpcb.nic.in and fssai.gov.in when the network is back). Status stays 'partly'; all snippet-based figures need the searches re-run once fetches work.
